small_guidance:
- Autotune the fused pool+post kernel over `num_warps ∈ {1, 2, 4}` and `num_stages ∈ {2, 3, 4}`; with C=16 (BLOCK_C=16) one warp per program is likely sufficient and reduces occupancy waste.
- Tile multiple output points per program (e.g. process 4 or 8 `(pd,ph,pw)` tuples per program along W_out) to amortize kernel launch and increase ILP, since each program currently only does 8 loads × 16 channels.
- Consider `channels_last_3d` memory layout for the conv output so the channel axis is contiguous; loads of all 16 channels at one spatial site collapse to a single 64-byte transaction.
large_guidance:
- The ConvTranspose3d dominates runtime (fast_p ≈ 0.29 means ~20.9 ms vs 6 ms baseline; the post-fusion is already cheap). Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton kernel implemented as scatter-add of `input × weight` outer products into the output grid (handle stride=2, padding=1, output_padding=1 in index math), and fuse the bias add into the same epilogue store.
- Alternatively, implement the transposed conv as a gather-style GEMM: one program per `(N, OC tile, D_out·H_out·W_out tile)`, looping over `(IC, kd, kh, kw)` with the standard transposed-conv index mapping `id = (od + pad - kd)/stride` (only when divisible). Use `BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32` as a starting tile and autotune.
- Fuse the entire pipeline end-to-end: conv-transpose epilogue writes directly into the maxpool→softmax→sub→swish→channel-max chain. With OC=16 the channel dim fits in registers, so a single persistent kernel per `(N, pooled-spatial)` tile that accumulates the conv output for all 16 channels at the 8 pre-pool sites, then performs pool+softmax+swish+max inline, eliminates the materialized conv output entirely.
